Reference.Title: A Patient With Pelizaeus-Merzbacher Disease Caused by a c.67G>A Mutation in the PLP1 Gene
Reference.Address: [Usman, Mohammad] Alabama Coll Osteopath Med, Psychiat & Behav Sci, Dothan, AL 36303 USA; [Koch, Alexis] Alabama Coll Osteopath Med, Internal Med, Dothan, AL USA; [Stolzenberg, Laurence] Alabama Coll Osteopath Med, Orthopaed Surg, Dothan, AL USA; [Huang, Austin] Alabama Coll Osteopath Med, Neurol, Dothan, AL USA; [Nkie, Veronica E.] Alabama Coll Osteopath Med, Gen Surg, Dothan, AL USA; [Ibrahim, Mohammad] Univ Cent Florida, Hlth Sci, Orlando, FL USA
Reference.Abstract: Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease is a tremendously rare genetic disorder caused by a mutation on the X chromosome. The mutation affects a gene critical to white matter myelination and results in significant neurological issues. Here, we present one such case of a child diagnosed with Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease. A relatively normal gestation and birth belied the underlying issue until he presented to the emergency department a month after birth with seizure-like activity and failure to thrive. After intensive evaluation and treatment, the patient was diagnosed with the illness and received surgery to place a tracheostomy and a gastrostomy tube to treat the stridor and failure to thrive caused by his illness. After approximately a month and a half of inpatient treatment, the patient was able to be discharged home in stable condition.
